major_concerns: External validity: digital-twin/emulator fidelity may not reflect real vendor quirks.
Validator-overfitting: repair loop can game validator outputs producing spurious passes (TOCTOU/coverage risk).
Prompt sensitivity could confound attribution of effects to validator fidelity rather than LLM variance.
Need clear artifact release plan to enable independent reproduction.
required_design_repairs: Include a validator-fidelity calibration step (show Batfish/emulator limitations vs. ground truth or multiple emulator versions).
Prespecify and publish topology corpus, prompts, seeds, and repair-prompt templates; provide scripts to replay runs.
Add monitoring for validator-overfitting (e.g., holdout semantic tests not exposed to repair loop).
Explicitly bound claims to tested LLM/model and synthetic topology scope.

major_concerns: Engineering risk: constrained-decoding integration with hosted LLM APIs can be nontrivial and brittle.
Schema design may bias results or omit vendor-specific constructs, inflating apparent semantic gains.
Digital-twin evaluation may misclassify vendor-correct but schema-omitted constructs as failures.
Need clearer operationalization of 'schema strictness' and decoder fallback policies.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact constrained-decoding implementation (token-level filter, constrained sampler, or post-hoc mapper) and fallbacks if the LLM violates schema.
Provide multiple schema strictness levels and document schema design rationale; publish schemas.
Include vendor-specific template extensions or a mechanism to encode vendor idioms and evaluate their effect.
Add sensitivity analyses for decoding temperature and schema strictness; preregister these comparisons.

major_concerns: Simulation realism: injected failures and rollback policies may not reflect operator behavior in production.
Canary threshold tuning risks overfitting to simulated failure distribution.
Need to avoid conflating simulator-detected ‘safe-deploy’ with real-world operational safety.
required_design_repairs: Document and publish the simulation model (failure injection types, timing/TOCTOU models, rollback policy) with replay scripts.
Include robustness checks: vary canary thresholds, injection rates, and rollback policies; report sensitivity.
Justify selection of injected failure types and proportion (40%) relative to operational data or prior literature.
Preregister decision rules for automated rollback and for what constitutes a ‘safe-deploy’ event.

major_concerns: Proof artifacts may be toy/over-simplified and not reflect deployable proof-carrying schemes; risk of overstating mitigation.
Adversarial-prompt experiments create ethical risk; must avoid publishing exploit recipes.
Protocol mediation may produce high false-rejection rates with operational costs that need quantification.
Executor enforcement in simulation may not map to real-world executors and admin policies.
required_design_repairs: Specify provably-structured proof format and verifier rules; avoid toy attestations or clearly label them as prototypes.
Define safe handling/redaction policy for adversarial prompts and do not include raw exploit prompts in public artifacts.
Measure and report false-rejection operational cost (delay, rollback overhead) and include human-override modeling.
Add qualitative analysis of failure cases where protocol mediation failed and tie them to concrete mitigations or limitations.
